assessment: Assignment changes and renames are associated with affected exports, but their causal role is unproved. Replacement delay and active handling also need separate measurement. Both openings retain private processing, the documented CSV, concurrent attendance entry, and the six-day/hosting ceiling.

openings.claim: Selecting courses through their relationship to the requested week could prevent omissions associated with using current instructor assignments.
openings.delta: Change the temporal representation from current assignment to center-course-week membership. Recompose the export by selecting authorized membership tuples, then joining attendance by stable course identity and emitting the existing CSV schema.
openings.prediction: If current-assignment selection causes omissions, an instructor handoff will change the incumbent course set but leave a correctly specified week-membership selection intact. Unchanged-assignment controls should agree.
openings.probe: In private staging, compare both selectors on fabricated handoffs, renames, and a split, including identical labels across centers and attendance entered during export. Compare stable IDs against coordinator-approved intended sets. Bound implementation to six engineer-days and existing hosting; proceed only if trustworthy membership history is available.
assumptions: Stable course identities and usable historical membership can be obtained within the budget.
Coordinators can resolve which split courses belong to a requested week.

openings.claim: Does a replacement cycle consume active coordinator effort, or mainly introduce elapsed waiting?
openings.delta: Represent each export as a handling trajectory. Recompose per-export handling time by summing active intervals for checking, requesting, downloading, correcting, and importing; record waiting separately.
openings.prediction: Waiting-dominated cycles would show long request-to-delivery gaps but little active replacement work; reconciliation-dominated cycles would show repeated schedule comparisons or spreadsheet corrections.
openings.probe: Use the six coordinators' two sessions with fabricated normal and affected exports to observe these intervals. If active replacement work dominates, test an authorized in-service rerun control; if comparison dominates, prioritize course-selection correction. Recheck the next 40 exports against all three success measures.
assumptions: Reduced waiting alone does not establish reduced handling time.
